data.body:
AC EVIDENCE, verified against merged main (Gerrit 2079).

AC1 predicate + parameters in their own module: the grep prints 3 (REPEAT_FIX_WINDOW_DAYS, REPEAT_FIX_MIN_PRIOR, def repeat_fix_escalates) in src/rebar/llm/code_review/repeat_fix.py.
AC2 new unit tests: 22 passed.
AC3 under-floor repeat-fix escalates: test_repeat_fix_escalates_an_under_floor_bug_fix passes.
AC4 existing gate behaviour preserved: 58 passed across test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py and test_bug_blast_radius_escalation_ad0d.py.
AC5 backtest emits the verdict from the SHIPPED predicate: --rev-range HEAD~200..HEAD --repeat-fix exits 0; 70 rows, every one carrying repeat_fix.
AC6 labelled recall per predicate: --rev-range origin/main --repeat-fix --labels-from-caused-by exits 0 and prints 'labelled 26 of 651; size recall 10/26 (38.5%) escalation 105/651; repeat-fix 12/26 (46.2%) escalation 228/651; union 14/26 (53.8%) escalation 254/651'. The criterion asks that the summary EXISTS and its floor row RECONCILES, not that digits are frozen - and it does: the floor still finds the same 10 labelled fixes recorded on 2026-08-21, with the labelled set having grown 22 -> 26 as history advanced.
AC8 docs: grep -c 'repeat-fix' docs/plan-review-gate.md prints 8, well over the required 2.

AC7 holds on the terms the criterion itself sets. --check-planning-corpus reports 'corpus=114 (want 113); missed=[]; mechanical_fp=[]; FAIL'. The criterion requires the two EMPTY lists - the flagged set is still exactly ADJUDICATED_SUBSTANTIVE - and explicitly names the count arm, 'corpus=114 (want 113) (exit 1)', as a PRE-EXISTING drift reproduced unchanged on pristine origin/main, tracked separately and out of scope. I ran it from a worktree reset --hard to origin/main with no local changes, so what I observed IS pristine main, which confirms that claim rather than taking it on trust.

Two defects in this change were found by review and CI rather than by me, and both were real: the gate evaluated the repeat-fix window at wall-clock now while the backtest passed the commit's timestamp (fixed by threading the anchor through escalation_for_diff and rewiring the backtest to call the GATE, not the predicate beneath it), and the new test built a raw {**os.environ, ...} mapping, which the repo forbids outside tests._subprocess_env.subprocess_env. My first fix for the latter used a tests.-rooted import that resolves under 'python -m pytest' but not under the bare 'pytest' CI runs - caught on all four shards, now the bare-name form.
